analysis.investment_thesis: Cemindia Projects (formerly ITD Cementation) is a specialized infrastructure contractor dominating complex niche work — marine structures, airport civils, tunnels — that perfectly aligns with India's multi-decade government capex supercycle. At a P/E of 23.7x against net profit growing ~36% YoY (FY25: ₹373 Cr vs FY24: ₹274 Cr), the PEG ratio of ~0.66 puts this squarely in Lynch's sweet spot.
key_strengths: Revenue nearly tripled from ₹3,809 Cr (FY22) to ₹9,097 Cr (FY25) — a 3-year CAGR of ~34% — powered by India's port, airport, and highway buildout
ROCE of 27.6% and ROE of 21.8% are excellent for a construction company, indicating high-quality project selection and execution
Debt/Equity of 0.48 is well within Lynch's 0.6 threshold, and cash of ₹358 Cr provides a reasonable buffer; OCF positive 5/5 years
key_risks: FY25 operating cash flow cratered to ₹203 Cr from ₹704 Cr in FY24 — construction cash flows are lumpy but this magnitude of swing warrants monitoring
Operating margin is thin at 7.74%; any project cost overruns, labour inflation, or client payment delays can rapidly compress profitability
Recent parent change to Renew Exim DMCC introduces ownership uncertainty — promoter strategy and capital allocation priorities are less proven under the new structure
red_flags: Free cash flow was only ₹30 Cr in FY25 despite ₹373 Cr net profit — significant working capital consumption typical of construction but limits financial flexibility
Capex was ₹228 Cr in FY25 while revenues rely heavily on government contract awards — any policy slowdown or election-cycle freeze on public spending directly hits order inflows
analysis.detailed_analysis:
This is the kind of company Lynch loved to find: a specialized niche operator in an industry with visible secular tailwinds that most investors find too dull to research properly. India is spending unprecedented sums on ports, airports, and metro rail — and Cemindia does the hard civil work nobody else in the country can match at scale. Revenue CAGR of ~34% over three years with improving ROCE is the fundamental story, and a PEG of 0.66 means I'm not overpaying for it.

The near-term cash flow lumpiness (FCF of just ₹30 Cr in FY25 versus ₹369 Cr in FY24) is the key watch item — this is inherent to the business model, not a structural breakdown. Forward P/E of 17.15 suggests the market already expects some growth deceleration, which is reasonable, but if the order book continues to compound with India's infra spending, this could be a solid multi-year compounder at current prices.
